Let \(m\geq7\) be an integer and write \([m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Define a finite simplicial complex \(K_m\) on the vertex set \(\{1,2,3,4\}\times[m]\) by declaring that a subset \(F\) is a face precisely when
\[
\left|F\cap(\{i\}\times[m])\right|\leq2\quad(i=1,2,3),\qquad
\left|F\cap(\{4\}\times[m])\right|\leq m-5,
\]
and
\[
\left|F\cap(\{1,2,3,4\}\times\{j\})\right|\leq1\quad(j\in[m]).
\]
For integers \(t\geq2\) and \(n\geq2\), let \(M(\mathbb Z/t\mathbb Z,n)\) denote the Moore space obtained from \(S^n\) by attaching one \((n+1)\)-cell along a map \(S^n\to S^n\) of degree \(t\). A wedge identifies chosen basepoints, and a wedge with zero summands is a point.

Determine the homotopy type of the geometric realization \(|K_m|\) for every \(m\geq7\), expressed as a finite wedge of spheres and Moore spaces, with every dimension, cyclic order, and multiplicity given explicitly as a function of \(m\).
</problem>

275	## 5. Why these homology groups determine the homotopy type here
276	
277	Two further points are needed: a dimension bound and simple connectivity.
278	
279	### Dimension bound
280	
281	Project the face poset onto its row-\(1,2,3\) part \(\sigma\). In the fiber over \(\sigma\), let \(j\) be the smallest unused column. Match a row-four face not containing \(j\) with the face obtained by adding \((4,j)\), whenever allowed.
282	
283	This matching is acyclic in each fiber, and hence acyclic on the whole face poset. Apart from the basepoint, its unmatched faces have:
284	
285	* \(s\leq4\) colored vertices;
286	* exactly \(k=m-5\) row-four vertices.
287	
288	Their dimensions are
289	\[
290	s+k-1\leq m-2.
291	\]
292	If \(s\geq5\), the row-four fiber is a full nonempty simplex and has no unmatched face. Discrete Morse theory therefore gives a CW model for \(K_m\) of dimension at most \(m-2\).
293	
294	### Simple connectivity
295	
296	Let \(J\) be the join of the \(m\) four-point column sets. It is simply connected. The complexes \(K_m\) and \(J\) have the same one-skeleton.
297	
298	A triangle of \(J\) missing from \(K_m\) consists of three vertices in a row whose capacity is two. Its boundary bounds a disk in \(K_m\): cone that boundary to a vertex in a different row and a column outside the triangle. All three cone triangles belong to \(K_m\).
299	
300	Thus adding the missing triangles does not change the fundamental group, and
301	\[
302	\pi_1(K_m)=\pi_1(J)=0.
303	\]
304	
305	By (14), reduced homology vanishes below dimension \(n=m-3\). The Hurewicz theorem, applied inductively, now shows that \(K_m\) is \((n-1)\)-connected. Its CW dimension is at most \(n+1\).
306	
307	Finally, an \((n-1)\)-connected CW complex of dimension at most \(n+1\), for \(n\geq2\), is a wedge of \(n\)-spheres, \((n+1)\)-spheres, and Moore spaces \(M(\mathbb Z/t,n)\). One way to see this is to use cellular cancellation to obtain cells only in dimensions \(0,n,n+1\). The attaching maps are then classified by an integer matrix, and integral changes of cellular bases put that matrix in Smith form.
308	
309	Applying this observation to (15) proves precisely (4).
